The pages give the rule. cli-cairn-json-output.md:25-26 says every payload except a per-site NDJSON line carries exitCode, and line 49 says stream site lines omit exitCode. The command the wrapper itself ran (with or without a site) also tells the two forms apart.

cli-cairn-exit-codes.md:95-97 lists every empty-stdout case (usage error, a run that ended before any payload, a tool fault), and each reports UNKNOWN. Lines 9-10 and 79-80 say these exit 3, so no documented case gives empty stdout with another code. The reader's worry is about a fact that does not exist.

cli-cairn-json-output.md:50 says a stream with no summary line reads UNKNOWN. cli-cairn-exit-codes.md:79-80 and 95-97 say a tool fault or a run that ended before its payload reports UNKNOWN (3). In the code, health_sweep.go:111-113 returns an error mid-stream, which is the tool-fault path; any other truncation is an external kill, whose exit code cairn does not set.

Keeping timestamps as strings is a typing choice. The reader based it on the documented rule that the zero time is written as an empty string (json-output.md:116), and makes no claim that the docs are wrong or silent.

No published page says whether an --expect-sites mismatch writes a payload or how the payload shows it. cli-cairn-json-output.md:299-302 ties `errors` only to registry reads that failed, and the exit-codes page (lines 7-8, 63) gives only the exit code 3. The code writes the payload and puts the mismatch in `errors` (tool/cmd/cairn/sites.go:80-88 and 145-149). I searched the full docs tree for 'expect' and found only the exit-code lines.

The claim assumes the job needed stdin behavior for --json commands, and that premise fails. cli-cairn-json-output.md:386 says the only password prompt is `cairn auth set`, which is not a --json command, so no --json run reads stdin.

The pages contradict each other. cli-cairn-json-output.md:346-348 says `adoptable` was added within schema version 1 and a reader written before it still reads every candidate. But the adopt-list schema, which line 38 calls normative, sets `additionalProperties: false` on each candidate (cairn-adopt-list.schema.json:20), so a reader following the pre-`adoptable` schema would reject the new field.

There is no contradiction. cairn-doctor.schema.json:28 lists the shared five-word state vocabulary, and cli-cairn-json-output.md:402-403 only says doctor never writes `held`. A schema that allows more than the command emits does not conflict with the page.

A looser schema is not a contradiction. cairn-doctor.schema.json:22 requires only checkId and state, while cli-cairn-doctor.md:95 and 109 say `condition` is always present and a fail carries a `fix`. Every payload the page describes still validates, so the two agree.

cairn-auth-check.schema.json:19-25 makes `reason` optional, and cli-cairn-json-output.md:375-376 says a row carries it beside anything other than a pass. The page adds a rule within what the schema allows, so there is no conflict.

The pages contradict each other. cli-cairn-doctor.md:121-122 says empty stdout under --json means the invocation was wrong and a usage error is 'the one case that writes no payload'. cli-cairn-exit-codes.md:95-97 says empty stdout can also come from a run that ended before any payload was written, or from a tool fault.
